description: ShadeWalk is a code base for city-scale mapping of artificial shade facilities, facility-aware shadow modelling and coolest-route pedestrian flow mapping, built for Singapore with Bologna as a second city for arcade detection. It is written by Shuyang Zhang of the National University of Singapore; version 1.0.6 was archived on Zenodo on 21 September 2026 and derives from a JOSS software paper. Five modules cover a GPU version of the SOLWEIG model with added shadow layers for facilities (13 shadow classes), covered-linkway extraction with GeoSAM and TopoLoRA including training data and a checkpoint, arcade detection in street-view imagery with CLIP projected onto footprints, pedestrian flow mapping with a coolest-route cost model and betweenness, and reconstruction of a shade-aware OpenStreetMap pedestrian network. Coverage: Singapore, with Bologna for arcades. Access: GitHub, Zenodo and figshare input data. Licence: MIT; free. Caveats: tuned to tropical and arcade-rich cities and needs GPU resources. Simulation uses: pedestrian heat exposure, shade planning and routing on hot days. Related records: the Vienna water features case study and the tree and building shading dataset.
